title: SE-bound release of the entropy halves on a firmware measurement: each SE releases its half only after the measured-boot digest matches a value sealed at first boot, so a glitched FSBL/MCU integrity check cannot unlock funds
threat: Donjon's Safe 3 result is the concrete 'malicious hardware/firmware in the MCU' case: SE pairing secrets prove possession of a key, not what code is running, so a glitch on the MCU's own integrity check yields a reprogrammed device that still passes SE attestation. pq1 is structurally the same: OPTIGA PBS / SE050 SCP03 keys are DHUK/BHK-derived and any code running on the die can recompute them; a glitched FSBL verify (or an RDP downgrade) therefore still reaches both halves after PIN.
proposal: At first boot (Phase B), seal `M0 = SHA-256(fingerprint_digest_slotA ‖ fingerprint_digest_slotB_or_empty ‖ fsbl_digest ‖ option_byte_profile)` into each SE: OPTIGA as an AuthRef/confidentiality-protected data object whose read of half_O requires a session bound to a HMAC(M_current) proof via Shielded Connection (or as a key-derivation input into the PBS-equivalent session), SE050 by binding the UserID-protected object policy to a `HMAC-SHA256(K_se050_meas, M_current)` presented as part of the SCP03 session key derivation. The secure world recomputes M_current every boot from measured_boot::run (not the FSBL, since the FSBL is pre-secret) and derives the per-boot session material from it; a wrong measurement produces an undecryptable half rather than a visible refusal. Legitimate A/B updates re-seal under the PIN-gated fw_commit path (COMMIT already requires unlock) by writing the new M under the old session before the boot pointer flips, with a journaled rollback. Pair with a C10 MCU attestation (fingerprint-signed challenge) for the companion.
rationale: Moves the trust anchor for fund release from 'the MCU's integrity check was not glitched' to 'the SEs saw the expected measurement', which no public attack on an SE-less path can forge without also faulting the SE policy; it is the only design that makes a successful RDP downgrade or FSBL-verify glitch insufficient on its own. Trezor's May-2026 ML-DSA MCU attestation shows vendors are moving toward measured-MCU evidence, but none bind the seed release to it.
repo_evidence: secure/src/dual_se.rs:461-477 (unlock cross-check is entropy→master self-consistency only; no measurement input)
secure/src/measured_boot.rs (advisory fingerprint; not consumed by any SE policy)
secure/src/hw/secret_keys.rs (PBS/SCP03 derive from DHUK+salt / BHK — possession keys, no code binding)
docs/security/threat-model.md (no SE-bound measurement entry); issue search 'measurement SE release' → none
vendor_precedent: None binds seed release to a firmware measurement. Nearest: Trezor mcu_attestation.c (ML-DSA MCU attestation for Suite, not for seed release); Ledger Secure Screen/Genuine Check attests the SE only.
risks: Touches invariants #1/#3 adjacent code (SE provisioning, S-1/S-2/S-3 OPTIGA lockdown is already a ship-blocker — this adds another object/policy to that ceremony); a fw_update that fails between re-seal and boot-pointer flip could brick (needs the journaled recovery proof the first-boot flow already lacks); the FSBL cannot participate (pre-secret, frozen), so the measurement is the secure world's — a fully compromised secure image could lie, which is why FI-03/FI-06 (FSBL + RDP integrity) remain load-bearing. Must stay SPHINCS+C10-only for any attestation signature.
